newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: HIGH COURT RULES AGAINST STATE TOBACCO CHARGES
The High Court has ruled that the New South Wales State Government's charges on tobacco sales are invalid.
The decision could leave a question mark over $5 billion worth of revenue collected by all Australian States on tobacco, petrol and alcohol.
In a majority judgment, the High Court ruled against the business franchise fees imposed by New South Wales on tobacco.
Two businesses challenged the right to levy the fee because it is paid as a percentage of sales.
The challenge came under Section 90 of the Constitution, which gives the Commonwealth the exclusive power to levy excise duties.
ENGINEERS TO TEST LAND MOVEMENT AT THREDBO RESCUE SITE
Engineers at Thredbo will conduct drilling tests today to determine the extent of land movement at the rescue site.
The search effort was suspended for three hours overnight after a large concrete slab slipped 30 centimetres, raising further concerns about the stability of the site.
The recovery operation has now resumed with reinforcements arriving from Sydney and country New South Wales.
Eight people are still missing beneath the debris.
Police Inspector Don Keene said the work by engineers today would greatly assist the rescue efforts.
"They'll be drilling to see just what the ground is doing," he said.
Meanwhile, the managing director of the Thredbo resort, David Osborne, said tourism had been unaffected by the tragedy.
Mr Osborne said the community relied on visitors for its survival.
"What we're saying is it is safe to come," he said.
"Please don't stay away; please don't think that the Thredbo community wants to be left on its own to deal with this tragedy.
"It's a community that's always existed for the enjoyment of the people who've come here, and that's their purpose for being here. To leave them on their own at this time isn't going to help at all."
SYSTEM FAILING THE POOR, HOUSING ASSISTANCE INQUIRY TOLD
Welfare groups have told the Federal Government's Inquiry into Housing Assistance the system is failing the poorest and most disadvantaged in the community.
The groups, including St Vincent de Paul, the Sydney City Mission and the Council of Social Service and Shelter, have painted a picture of increasing hardship for those who need housing assistance.
They said rising rents, particularly in Sydney, and increasing poverty were putting futher strain on the system.
They have told the inquiry it would be disastrous for the Federal Government to wind back its commitment to providing public housing in favour of increasing private sector involvement.
Among the reforms they have recommended were targetting negative gearing towards those providing affordable housing, and restructuring rent assistance to take account of high-cost city living.
GOVT'S IMMUNISATION SHOCK CAMPAIGN CALLED A "FARCE"
The Federal Government's campaign to increase the level of immunisation has been described as a farce.
Kathy Scarborough, the co-ordinator of a South Australian group, Vaccination Information, said the Commonwealth was using a shock campaign that told parents only part of the story.
A baby boy in a whooping cough spasm features in a television advertisement that began screening this week.
Ms Scarborough said while whooping cough was a dangerous disease, South Australian statistics showed vaccination was not working as well as the Government was trying to convey.
She said the Government was not telling people that while there were more than 1000 cases of whooping cough last year, 51 per cent of those with the disease had been fully vaccinated.
That suggested that if the vaccine had worked at all, its effects had worn off over time.
INDUSTRY SAYS CABINET SHOULD NOTE MORE TOURISTS MEANS MORE JOBS
The Federal Government should take into account the tourism industry's strong job-creation record when Cabinet meets today, according to a major tourism body.
Cabinet is meeting in Sydney to discuss Australia's unemployment problem.
Inbound Tourism managing director Len Taylor said jobs growth in the tourism industry continued to outshine that in any other.

Mr Taylor said the Government should examine incentives to foster that jobs growth, such as trainee and apprentice schemes. He said latest Bureau of Statistics figures show the industry created more than 17,500 jobs in 1996-97, based on a model which indicated every 16 tourists create one new job.
SECOND CRISIS MEETING PLANNED OVER ABORIGINAL DEATHS
An unusually large number of deaths in South Australia's Aboriginal community will be the subject of a second crisis meeting in Adelaide on Friday.
The State chairman of the Aboriginal Justice Advisory Committee, Tauto Sansbury, said he was concerned about the number of deaths outside of custody - an estimated 35 to 40 in the past two months.

He said last year's figures were also too high. About 133 Aborigines died in South Australia in 1996, even though Aborigines comprise less than one per cent of the State's population of about 1,428,000.
Mr Sansbury said something must be done because many of the deaths involved people aged between 20 and 40, some involved drugs and alcohol, and many were preventable.
"We've had a couple that have been suicides, there's been two hangings, a shooting, a heroin overdose and there's been a lot of other deaths that I believe have been preventable deaths," he said.
"The Aboriginal people are not accessing the health system and a lot of Aboriginal people are dying through that."
CATHY FREEMAN'S WIN AN INSPIRATION FOR KIDS - AND HER MUM
Cathy Freeman's world championship win is an inspiration for young Australian athletes and a fantastic pointer to the 2000 Games, according to New South Wales Olympics Minister Michael Knight.
Freeman won the 400 metre title at the World Athletics Championships in Athens this morning.
She said she is looking forward to getting back to Australia to share her victory and her medal with her mother.
Freeman said her mother had seemed more excited about the win than she herself was.
She said the run was not one of her best but was a fantastic result after a hard year.
SUSSEX CONFIRMS BIG OFFER TO SHANE WARNE
Struggling English county cricket club Sussex has confirmed it has made a big offer to Australian leg-spinner Shane Warne.
Warne is not expected to make a decision on the one-year offer until the end of the current Ashes tour.
Sussex chief executive Tony Pigot said securing Warne's services would be a huge boost to the club.
"I think Shane Warne brings a lot more than just being a cricketer on the pitch. I think he's a tremendous personality," Mr Pigot said.
"Hopefully, the membership would increase and everybody would come and watch us."
